decision: Close KIOTA-RECURSOR-TYPE-REPAIR-1 with a validated source repair, exact offline regression evidence and an indexed but unsubmitted local PR draft. Select TRUST-ASSUMPTION-PIPELINE-PILOT-1 READY and unstarted for its source/reuse assessment and staged protocol-binding phase because it is the highest-ranked unfinished local discovery item and can reuse existing axiom/reporting assets without a scientific launch.

categories.assessment: The recursor trust path now has a tested production repair package at the pinned source. The next distinct frontier question is whether validation reports preserve transitive trust assumptions across two supported paths; source and protocol binding can proceed before experimental execution.

The completed Kiota patch, full-suite evidence and local PR draft are reusable maintenance assets. Existing axiom and reporting tooling makes the assumption-preservation protocol the most direct next shared conformance asset, while the stateful pilot still lacks public session and rollback contracts.

The Kiota source patch remains local because current-tip, duplicate and maintainer-capacity context was not refreshed and no external submission was authorized. No further upstream action is part of this handoff; the next selected item is local research preparation.

The selected assumption-reporting item can begin by auditing retained toolchain trust mechanisms and reusing existing axiom/comparator/report paths. The stateful alternative needs a separate contract survey before its six request histories can be frozen.

The assumption-reporting item's immediate source/reuse and protocol-binding phase is feasible locally and removes its launch gate without starting scientific execution. The stateful pilot remains blocked from promotion until supported session, termination, rollback, fresh-name and dependency-order contracts are established.

candidates.rationale: READY and unstarted for a source/reuse assessment and staged protocol binding. Existing retained axiom and report tooling supports this preparatory phase; exact fixtures, expected transitive sets and observable paths must be committed before any launch.

The request-history question remains useful but cannot yet be promoted because its supported session boundary and failure-recovery contract are not established; it is less immediately reusable than the assumption-reporting protocol.

blockers.reason: Establish supported public session, termination, rollback, fresh-name and dependency-order contracts before freezing the six request histories.
